items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: John Collins on guitar, just with the 8 piece group, we made that 'Further Definitions.'

ctx.x: Field, mentioned to me -- he'd like me to, you know, just use the saxophone section and recreate a couple of things that Coleman Hawkins and I had done in Paris many years earlier with the two French saxophone players, Andre Ekyan, the altoist, and Alex Combelle, who is a tenor saxophone player; so we got together, oh, Phil Woods on the other alto and Charlie Rouse on the other tenor, Coleman Hawkins, myself -- with Jimmy Garrison on base and Dick Katz on piano, and Joe Jones on drums and John Collins on guitar,…
And you did a few of the tunes of those famous brase.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I recorded with Benny Carter... Benny Carter was the leader, and it was Georgie Auld... So I was in New York in later years and Benny Carter was there to do some recording, so he called me to do this recording with him.

ctx.x: 'I Hear Music', oh, it was just a great album, great album. And let's see, during that time I recorded with Benny Carter, and I did quite a few recordings with Fletcher during that time. I was speaking of Fletcher. I want to give you the personnel of this band. This was -- had a trombone player, Claude -- wait a minute. Sandy Williams, and we had a trumpet player, Joe Keyes, who was a great trumpet player. These guys were older than I was and they really taught me the business about band, you know, big band…

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Right, and I think John Collins.
